eyebrow: A WORD GAME FOR PEOPLE YOU KNOW
headline:
A little wordplay.
A little closer.
intro: A shared table, a handful of letters, and a reason to spend a little time together. Made for my family. Ready for yours.
availability: Available to play in your browser. The game opens in a new tab.
story: I made this for my grandma and sister: a familiar word-tile game they could share, even when they were in different places. The point is not another app to keep up with. It is another way to stay in touch.
features: Build words across the board and play with someone you know.
Open the game on a phone, tablet, or computer.
A personal project, built around the people who will actually use it.

headline:
A familiar game.
Your own quiet moment.
intro: Good cards. Comfortable controls. A table that feels like home. Solitaire Clemulie is the game I made for my grandma.
availability: Available to play in your browser. The game opens in a new tab.
storyTitle: Named for my grandma. Built for another hand.
story: The details matter when you play every day: the feel of moving a card, the space around the controls, the familiar rhythm of Klondike. That is where I have put the care.
features: A familiar card game, without turning it into something else.
Designed around readable cards and satisfying movement.
Built as a progressive web app for returning to the game.

headline:
Give your time
a little more intention.
intro: An app-blocking project built around the schedule you choose, not another feed asking for your attention.
availability: In development. There is no public app download yet.
storyTitle: The schedule should do the remembering.
story: blockApp explores dependable blocking and clear escape controls. The aim is a tool that supports a decision you have already made about your day.
features: Set the structure for your day rather than deciding again every time.
Blocking and escape controls are being developed together.
Built in Kotlin, with the native behaviour still being tested.

headline:
Start with
“What should I watch?”
intro: A remote-friendly player for your own playlists and programme guides. A better way to browse, without supplying the channels.
availability: In development. No public download, TV channels, or subscriptions are offered here.
story: tvapp is a player-interface project for Google TV and Android. It starts with the experience of sitting back with a remote and finding something worth watching.
features: A layout designed for directional controls and a television screen.
The player works toward supporting user-supplied playlists and guides.
The screenshot shows a native development build and test content.

headline:
Keep the session
in view.
intro: An observational dashboard concept for Whatnot sellers: totals, buyer activity, estimated fees, and exports in one useful place.
availability: Prototype. There is no public extension install link yet.
story: ShowTally is designed to observe a live selling session, not bid or post on anyone’s behalf. The project explores what a seller needs to see while the session is moving.
features: A concise view of activity during a selling session.
A place to understand the working numbers, using sample data here.
A prototype workflow for taking the session figures with you.

headline:
A home-court
advantage.
intro: A black-and-gold direction for a basketball coaching website in Barrie. Programme information, made easy to find.
availability: Design concept only. This is not a live coaching or booking service.
story: The concept gives the coaching programme room to speak for itself: clear programme cards and a mobile-friendly layout. This page documents the design direction, not a launched client website.
features: A concept that puts training information ahead of visual clutter.
A direction designed around someone looking for a programme on a phone.
The visual is a design study, not a screenshot of a launched service.

headline:
A clearer way
to compare nearby.
intro: A working-title exploration of local rankings, bringing review volume and average rating into one browsing experience.
availability: In development. Not a launched directory; the prototype uses sample data.
story: Ratings Explorer investigates a useful way to compare local categories in Barrie and Ottawa–Gatineau. The current interface is an Astro prototype, not a live source of business rankings.
features: A focused view of places around you.
Exploring how volume and average rating can work together.
The screenshot was rendered locally without an external ratings API.

headline:
Music, one
synthesized note at a time.
intro: Lo-fi experiments made with Node.js: an original composition, instrument studies, and another way to use code as a creative tool.
availability: Creative experiment. Audio is not published on this page.
story: Harbor Lights began as an original composition in code. This project collects that experiment alongside instrument studies. The pictured waveform was measured from the original audio, not drawn as decoration.
features: Harbor Lights is part of this collection of experiments.
Explorations of the sounds that form the music.
Written in Node.js, with audio synthesis at the centre.

headline:
Make the what-ifs
easier to see.
intro: A private household budgeting and scenario-planning project. A way to reason about shared bills and changes to a plan.
availability: Private tool. No public app, personal financial figures, or financial advice are provided here.
storyTitle: A private workspace for better questions.
story: This page is an overview of the idea. It does not expose the working dashboard, household information, or personal projections. The image is explicitly a concept illustration.
features: A dashboard concept for bills and a financial plan.
Exploring how a changed assumption affects the picture.
Only a high-level project description appears in this portfolio.

headline:
A small experiment
in comparison.
intro: One of the early projects in this collection: a single-page exploration of aggregating shoe ratings.
availability: Research and web experiment. Public source is available; there is no separate app release.
storyTitle: Small projects are part of the process.
story: Shoe Ratings belongs to the earlier experiments that helped start this portfolio. It is kept here as a record of learning by building, not presented as a current product-rating authority.
features: A study of how collected ratings could be presented.
The original public repository can be explored separately.
